metadata.description: Small Claude Code tools and skills by Mark Henry.

plugins.name: quota
plugins.description: Weekly quota left on Claude and ChatGPT subscriptions behind CLIProxyAPI vs an even-spend target, plus automatic account-weight rebalancing.

plugins.name: video
plugins.description: Download and clip videos with yt-dlp and ffmpeg, including past windows of streams that are still live.

plugins.name: flights
plugins.description: Scrape the Google Flights price calendar (cheapest fare per day across months) via browser-use.

plugins.name: gordian
plugins.description: Big-picture simplification audit for code that has accumulated complexity from many small edits.

plugins.name: figure
plugins.description: Turn a result into a self-contained figure: the claim as title, a qualifying caption, then the chart.

plugins.name: naming
plugins.description: Choose a name that travels: state its job, list the siblings it must not be confused with, brainstorm widely, test candidates against the classic rules, recommend one.

plugins.name: evals
plugins.description: LLM eval hygiene: build-judge (build and validate an LLM judge: Hamel Husain's evals-skills procedure plus house rules, TPR/TNR on a held-out split), spot-check (a subagent reads a stratified high/middle/low sample of scored items and flags scores too high, too low or broken, before a human looks) and tune-prompt (tune a new prompt-driven component live, one case at a time: sealed prediction, run, blind human verdict scored against the agent's sealed bet, log, change the prompt on patterns).

plugins.name: decide
plugins.description: Reach a decision with fresh agents, or with the user. draftoff: three drafts of a document on different organizing ideas, grafted, then picked blind against a plain default draft. docket: present the user one decision at a time, each with the context needed to decide.

plugins.name: check
plugins.description: Can this be trusted? eyebrow: before work starts on a plan, ask who has tried it and what happened; a fresh agent on the strongest model says what the people who know the area best would say, and a web search looks for the case against.

plugins.name: unattended
plugins.description: Run work unattended and trust the result. interview: question the user until they have decided what they want, then freeze it as a written brief an unattended run can build against. go: carry a frozen brief to a checked result inside the approved cap, with proof of done and the user's decisions last. arbiter: keep the judge of done out of the worker's reach, with the arbiter-loop script on PATH.

plugins.name: lab
plugins.description: ML-lab rigor. experiment: standard checks for a single experiment (fine-tune, RL, LLM eval or judge, skill test): fourteen lines (raw items read, intended n scored, a scorer that fails a broken output, a reproduced baseline, the independent unit, one metric written before scoring, pilot power, saturated items, test touched once, run ids on every number, no leakage, trivial-policy floors, data recomputed per arm, a raised eyebrow at the design); prereg.py stamps each run under git and refuses the label counted when a line fails; and a fresh-agent sign-off for numbers that leave your hands.

plugins.name: upstream
plugins.description: Send a pull request to a repo someone else owns: read its CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, README and contributing guide before writing any commit, check that the PR is wanted, match the project's commit and PR conventions, run its checks, and show the user the draft before opening it.
